Surah 103 (Al-'Asr), Makkan.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1–3} The Exalted swears by al-'Asr (the time), which is the night and the day, the arena of the actions and deeds of the servants, that every human being is in loss. The one who loses is the opposite of the one who profits, and loss has many levels that vary: it may be absolute loss, like the state of one who loses this world and the Hereafter, who misses out on bliss and deserves the Blazing Fire.

And it may be loss in some respects and not in others. For this reason Allah made loss general to every human being, except for those who are characterized by four qualities:

Faith (iman) in what Allah has commanded belief in. Faith cannot exist without knowledge ('ilm); it is a branch of it that cannot be complete without it.

And righteous deeds (al-'amal al-salih), which encompass all acts of goodness, outward and inward, related to the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants, obligatory and recommended.

And mutual exhortation to truth, which is faith and righteous deeds; that is, some of them enjoin on one another that, urge one another to it, and encourage one another toward it.

And mutual exhortation to patience: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from the disobedience of Allah, and patience in the painful decrees of Allah. By the first two matters the servant perfects himself, and by the last two he perfects others. By perfecting these four matters, the servant has been saved from loss and has attained the great profit.
